key_headlines.title: Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hyung-il on US Nuclear Energy and Housing Prices
key_headlines.summary: Finance Minister Lee stated that US nuclear energy projects must meet domestic procedures and commercial viability before fund transfers, while expressing concern about Seoul's rising housing prices amid increased construction permits and approvals.

key_headlines.title: Skyrocketing Monthly Rent in Seoul's Study Districts: 100 Million Won for 30 Square Meters
key_headlines.summary: Small officetel units under 30 square meters in Seoul have seen monthly rents exceed 1 million won increase sixfold over five years, with youth bearing an increasingly heavy housing burden.

key_headlines.title: Samsung Electronics Results in Focus Amid High Interest Rates
key_headlines.summary: Market attention centers on Samsung Electronics' performance and whether the company can overcome high interest rate burdens, with KOSPI closing at 7003.74 and the won-dollar exchange rate at 1350.6 won.

key_headlines.title: Jeonse Fraud Victims to Receive Minimum One-Third of Deposits
key_headlines.summary: Starting November 13, victims of jeonse fraud can receive minimum support and advance payments guaranteeing one-third of their deposit recovery through applications to LH within a 90-day notification period.

key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Lee Prioritizes Livelihood Stability and Potential Growth Rate Enhancement
key_headlines.summary: The Finance Minister announced plans to strengthen housing, employment, and financial support for ordinary citizens while promoting 1.19 million public housing units and advancing Korea-US strategic investment cooperation.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea faces significant economic challenges as housing affordability worsens with monthly rents for small units surpassing 1 million won and youth facing unprecedented rental burden. The government is implementing comprehensive support measures including jeonse fraud victim protections and expanded public housing supplies. Deputy Prime Minister Lee emphasized the need to stabilize livelihoods while enhancing potential growth rates through improved housing access, job creation, and financial support programs. The focus remains on balancing policies to support ordinary citizens while maintaining macroeconomic stability amid global uncertainties.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The World Bank upgraded East Asia's 2026 growth forecast to 4.5%, attributed partly to strong AI export performance, though acknowledging potential slowdown risks as global central banks maintain higher interest rates. South Korea's fiscal authorities are addressing structural challenges including IMF's revised current account assessment model, which may disadvantageously impact Korea's economic evaluations despite strong semiconductor export performance. Government spending initiatives include increased public housing supply of 1.19 million units and infrastructure investments, while managing the fiscal implications of jeonse fraud victim compensation. The administration faces challenges in revenue distribution, with 63 trillion won in excess tax revenue requiring careful allocation between competing policy priorities.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI fell below 7,000 points as foreign investors sold shares, though US markets demonstrated resilience with the Nasdaq reaching all-time highs despite rising Treasury yields. AI-related stocks remained strong drivers of US market gains, with major tech companies posting record valuations amid expectations for the Federal Reserve's September FOMC meeting minutes. Bitcoin climbed to the 85,000 dollar range, reflecting broader risk appetite in crypto markets. Market participants await the Fed's September FOMC meeting records expected October 7th to gauge future interest rate policy direction and assess corporate earnings prospects beginning the following week.
sections.Industry & Technology: Hyundai Motor Group's electric vehicle shipments surged 20.4% in the first eight months, supporting Korea's EV market growth while Korean battery manufacturers' global market share declined 3.9 percentage points. DGIST announced a breakthrough passive cooling technology using atmospheric moisture to manage thermal issues in EV batteries, AI data centers, and mobile devices, addressing critical heat management challenges. The southwestern region is emerging as Korea's secondary semiconductor production hub, leveraging abundant renewable energy resources with power self-sufficiency reaching 213.4% and surplus renewable energy capacity at 53.1%. Energy infrastructure optimization remains critical for supporting advanced semiconductor manufacturing and emerging high-tech industries in underdeveloped regions.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment prices achieved record-high 86-week consecutive increases, though emerging downward signals appeared in traditionally bullish Gangnam areas and Yongsan district showing price adjustments. Small officetel units under 30 square meters experienced dramatic rent increases, with monthly payments exceeding 1 million won becoming increasingly common, particularly near universities where some units command 1.2 million won monthly. The government's special legislation for jeonse fraud victims guarantees minimum one-third deposit recovery starting November 13, providing critical protection amid widespread fraud incidents. LH launched dormitory-style jeonse rental programs with 500 units, including 200 units for Seoul National University, addressing acute youth housing shortages and supporting university infrastructure needs.
sections.International Economy: US markets demonstrated strength with the Nasdaq reaching all-time highs driven by AI sector enthusiasm, despite significant Treasury yield increases signaling potential inflation concerns. Market anticipation centers on the Federal Reserve's September FOMC meeting minutes scheduled for release October 7th, which may clarify the central bank's future rate trajectory and address October rate-hike expectations. Bitcoin surged to 85,000 dollars amid broader risk-on sentiment in international markets, reflecting investor confidence despite macroeconomic uncertainties. Global semiconductor and AI hardware manufacturers continue benefiting from sustained demand, though concerns persist regarding Treasury yield impacts on technology equity valuations and corporate profitability.
sections.AI & Economy: AI-related companies experienced mixed performance as strong infrastructure investment demand contrasted with rising operational costs; Naver's target price was downgraded due to slowing advertising and commerce revenue growth coupled with increased AI infrastructure investments. Southeast Asian nations face policy challenges as rapid AI data center expansion strains power and water resources, prompting regulatory reviews and community opposition to previously welcomed foreign investment. Japan is reviving aging coal power plants through capacity market mechanisms to support accelerating AI power demand while developing cleaner long-term energy infrastructure. Major Korean construction firms like Daewoo Engineering prioritize AI infrastructure expansion and profitability enhancement as core strategic objectives, reflecting sector-wide recognition of AI's transformative economic impact.
sections.Others: The government increased whistleblower rewards for preventing wage payment fraud from 100 million to 200 million won, addressing concerning 29.7% recovery rates that strain the wage guarantees fund. Japan adopts cautious approach toward Alaska LNG projects amid inflation and tariff concerns that could increase project costs and energy prices, with US Vice President Vance indicating coordination with South Korea on final decisions. Daejeon-Chungbuk region secured major economic achievements including multi-purpose synchrotron accelerator project launch, 5 trillion won financial cooperation with Korea Export-Import Bank, and 103.7 trillion won in investment commitments. Real estate services firm JLL Korea completed advisory work for Dongyang Life Insurance's office property sales across Ilsan, Daegu, and Ulsan locations as part of broader institutional portfolio restructuring.
